Law_Text: Consumer rights include the right to be protected against the marketing of goods, products or services which are hazardous to life and property, and the right to seek redressal against unfair trade practice.
Action_Steps: File a formal complaint on the National Consumer Helpline (1915) or e-Daakhil portal with your invoice.

Law_Text: A product seller or manufacturer shall be liable in a product liability action if the product contains a manufacturing defect or deviates from express warranty, entitling the consumer to replacement or full refund.
Action_Steps: Send a legal notice or formal email to customer support citing Section 84, demanding a refund within 15 days.

Law_Text: The Central Authority may issue directions and penalties up to 10 lakh rupees against any false or misleading advertisement that is prejudicial to the interest of any consumer.
Action_Steps: Take screenshots of the misleading ad and report it on the GAMA portal or National Consumer Helpline.

Law_Text: Whoever, by means of any communication device or computer resource, cheats by personation (phishing, fake calls, OTP fraud) shall be punished with imprisonment up to three years and fine up to one lakh rupees.
Action_Steps: Immediately call 1930 (National Cyber Crime Helpline) and file a report at cybercrime.gov.in within 24 hours.

Law_Text: Any intermediary or person who, while providing services under a lawful contract, discloses personal information without consent with intent to cause wrongful loss shall be punished with imprisonment up to three years.
Action_Steps: Send a grievance email to the company's Data Protection Officer (DPO) and file an IT adjudication complaint.

Law_Text: A landlord cannot unlawfully lock out a tenant, cut off essential supplies like electricity and water, or evict a tenant without serving a prior written notice as stipulated in the tenancy agreement.
Action_Steps: Approach the local Rent Authority or file a police complaint if essential utilities (water/power) are cut off.

Law_Text: Every employer is required to constitute an Internal Committee (IC) at each office to receive and redress complaints of sexual harassment from women at the workplace.
Action_Steps: Submit a written complaint to the Internal Committee (IC) of your company within 3 months of the incident.

Law_Text: A public servant who accepts or obtains an undue advantage (bribe) as a motive for doing or forbearing to do an official act is punishable with imprisonment.
Action_Steps: Report the demand to the Central Vigilance Commission (CVC) or the local Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) with proof.

Law_Text: A citizen can request information from a public authority by filing an application with the designated Public Information Officer (PIO) along with the prescribed fee.
Action_Steps: File an RTI application online via rtionline.gov.in or send it via registered post to the PIO of the concerned department.

Law_Text: Driving a two-wheeled motor cycle in a public place without wearing protective headgear (helmet) is a punishable offence under the act.
Action_Steps: Pay the fine via the local traffic police portal (Parivahan) or contest the challan in the local traffic court.

Law_Text: An aggrieved woman can file an application before the Magistrate seeking protection orders, residence orders, or monetary relief against domestic violence.
Action_Steps: Approach the local Protection Officer or file a complaint directly before the Judicial Magistrate.

Law_Text: Whoever commits theft shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or both.
Action_Steps: File an FIR at the nearest police station immediately with details of the stolen property.

Law_Text: Threatening another person with injury to their person, reputation, or property, with intent to cause alarm, is a punishable offence.
Action_Steps: File a police complaint (FIR) detailing the threats and provide evidence (screenshots, call recordings) to the police.

Law_Text: An act that causes common injury, danger, or annoyance to the public (e.g., illegal dumping, extreme noise) is considered a public nuisance.
Action_Steps: File a written complaint with the local municipal corporation or the nearest police station.

Law_Text: Using deceptive design patterns (dark patterns) to manipulate consumer choices or force them into making unintended purchases is an unfair trade practice.
Action_Steps: Report the specific website or app to the National Consumer Helpline (1915) or the Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA).

Law_Text: Whoever by words, either spoken or intended to be read, or by signs or by visible representations, makes or publishes any imputation concerning any person intending to harm their reputation commits defamation.
Action_Steps: Send a cease and desist legal notice or file a criminal defamation complaint before the Magistrate.

Law_Text: Where any cheque drawn by a person for the discharge of any debt or liability is returned by the bank unpaid due to insufficient funds, it constitutes an offence.
Action_Steps: Send a legal demand notice to the defaulter within 30 days of the cheque return memo, and file a case in court if unpaid after 15 days.

Law_Text: No child below the age of fourteen years shall be employed to work in any factory or mine or engaged in any other hazardous employment.
Action_Steps: Report the violation to the local police or the Labour Department immediately; you can also call the Childline helpline at 1098.

Law_Text: Taking or giving dowry directly or indirectly from the parents or guardians of a bride or bridegroom is a punishable offence with imprisonment of up to five years.
Action_Steps: File an FIR at the local police station or contact the Dowry Prohibition Officer in your district.

Law_Text: Any man who follows a woman and contacts, or attempts to contact such woman to foster personal interaction repeatedly despite a clear indication of disinterest commits stalking.
Action_Steps: File an FIR at the nearest police station or lodge a complaint on the National Cyber Crime portal if done online.

Section: Food Safety and Standards Act 2006 Sec 59
Law_Text: Any person who manufactures, sells, or distributes any article of food which is unsafe or adulterated shall be punished with imprisonment and a heavy fine.
Action_Steps: File a complaint on the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) portal or call the local food safety officer.

Law_Text: Deficiency in service includes any fault, imperfection, or shortcoming in the quality, nature, or manner of performance required to be maintained by a medical practitioner or hospital.
Action_Steps: Gather all medical records, take a second medical opinion, and file a complaint before the Consumer Commission.

Section: Indian Penal Code Sec 304A & Clinical Establishments Act
Law_Text: Refusing emergency medical treatment to a critical patient is a violation of the right to life and can result in criminal negligence charges against the hospital.
Action_Steps: Complain to the Chief Medical Officer (CMO) of the district or file a police complaint against the hospital administration.

Law_Text: The permissible noise limit for residential areas is 55 decibels during the day and 45 decibels at night. Loudspeakers cannot be used without written permission.
Action_Steps: Call the local police station to register a noise complaint; if the police do not act, file a complaint with the State Pollution Control Board.

Section: Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act 1960
Law_Text: While local authorities are responsible for managing stray populations, individual citizens cannot relocate, harm, or poison stray dogs; they have a right to live.
Action_Steps: Complain to the local Municipal Corporation for sterilization/vaccination drives; contact an animal welfare NGO or People for Animals (PFA).

Law_Text: Organizations must obtain explicit consent before collecting personal data and must implement reasonable security safeguards to prevent data breaches.
Action_Steps: File a complaint with the Data Protection Board of India (DPBI) and issue a legal notice to the company for damages.

Law_Text: A workman cannot be terminated from service without a valid reason, proper inquiry, or without providing the mandatory notice period or retrenchment compensation.
Action_Steps: Send a legal notice to the HR department and, if unresolved, approach the Labour Commissioner or the Labour Court.

Law_Text: Builders must adhere strictly to the completion date specified in the agreement. If they fail to deliver possession on time, the buyer is entitled to interest or a full refund.
Action_Steps: File a complaint with the State Real Estate Regulatory Authority (RERA) of your state.

Section: UP Prohibition of Unlawful Conversion of Religion Act 2021
Law_Text: No person shall convert or attempt to convert, either directly or otherwise, any other person from one religion to another by use of force, allurement, or fraudulent means.
Action_Steps: File an FIR at the nearest police station if you or someone you know is being coerced.

Law_Text: Cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property (like fake investment schemes or crypto apps promising guaranteed returns) is a punishable offence.
Action_Steps: Report immediately to the Economic Offences Wing (EOW) of the police or register a complaint at cybercrime.gov.in.

Law_Text: The Passport Authority cannot arbitrarily delay or reject a passport application without providing a written reason, provided all documents and police verifications are clear.
Action_Steps: File a grievance on the Passport Seva portal; if unresolved, send a legal notice or approach the High Court.
